before.beta: From Gladys Divide beyond Flapjack Lakes, the standard approach climbs a steep snow/scree gully to Needle Pass - icy and typically needing crampons and an axe into midsummer. A climbers'/goat trail then bypasses The Needle and Castle Spires along loose, exposed class 3-4 terrain to the notch south of The Horn. Do not underestimate The Horn as a simple scramble: despite the modest 5.5 grade, the final summit pitch is run-out and the rock demands careful gear placement.

approach_variants.name: Sawtooth crest traverse under The Fin's west face
approach_variants.notes: Same long walk in as the rest of the ridge: Staircase, the North Fork Skokomish, the steep haul to Flapjack Lakes, and up to Gladys Divide, with a reserved overnight permit for the lakes basin arranged well in advance. From the divide the tread turns primitive and you gain the crest through a steep snow-and-scree gully that commonly holds ice into midsummer, so an axe and crampons earn their weight on an early trip. A climbers' and goat path then works along the crest, circumventing the Needle and the Castle Spires on loose, exposed class 3-4 ground. Do not read the modest grade as a scramble — the summit pitch is run-out and the rock wants careful placements. Confirm the Skokomish approach trails are open before you go; fire damage has closed them for long stretches.
approach_variants.season: Late July to September; ice in gullies
hazards: Run-out, sparsely protected fifth-class climbing on the summit pitch — not a route to fall on
Rock quality falls off steadily as you move toward Sawtooth Pass, and worsens as snow melts off the ledges
The traverse under The Fin's west face is exposed and loose, with poor footing and nothing to catch a slip
Two ropes are wanted for the rappel back into the notch, and the anchors are slung rather than bolted
Slide alder and devil's club on any off-crest return line
Very long and remote — any rescue would take days, so carry a satellite communicator
approach_variants.baseFinding: The Horn is the next tower southeast beyond The Fin, and the climbing starts from the notch immediately south of it, not from the crest on either side. Coming along the goat path from the Needle and Castle Spires, you pass under The Fin's west face on an exposed loose traverse and drop into a small saddle floored with broken pillow basalt; the wall rising directly out of the far side of that saddle is The Horn. Two lines leave it — one up the steep, exposed southeast side and one on the west face — and both start off the notch floor rather than from any ledge above it. The tell that you are in the right saddle is what is behind you: the tower you have just walked under is slotted by a deep chimney, which is The Fin and nothing else on the ridge. If the tower above you carries that chimney, you are one notch short. If the crest ahead has eased and broadened toward Mount Lincoln with no steep blade left above you, you have gone past.

pitch_detail.notes: Loose, exposed climbers'/goat trail bypassing The Needle and Castle Spires
pitch_detail.pitch: Approach scramble (Needle/Sawtooth Pass to Horn's notch)

pitch_detail.notes: ~130 ft; standard alpine rack; An impressive powering mass of stone - don't let the modest grade cause overconfidence

before.turnaround: Turn back if the Needle Pass gully is icy or unconsolidated without the party carrying axes/crampons, if weather is deteriorating (Olympic alpine weather shifts quickly), or if the remaining daylight isn't enough to finish the exposed ridge scrambling, the technical notch pitch, and the long descent back to Flapjack Lakes before dark.
before.detailed_rack: A standard alpine trad rack (small-to-medium nuts and cams) covers the short technical pitch at The Horn's notch; long slings help manage rope drag on the wandering line. Crampons and an ice axe are recommended for the Needle Pass approach gully outside of late summer.

climate.fall: Conditions deteriorate through September-October as the first snow arrives
climate.spring: Snow lingers in the Needle Pass gully and on the ridge into June
climate.summer: Warmest, driest window (Jul-early Sep); roughly 5 rain days per month; wildflowers in bloom
climate.winter: Heavy snow; not a season for this route
climate.typical: Wet, mild winters and warmer, drier summers typical of the SE Olympics; snow can linger in the Sawtooth Pass/Gladys Divide approach gullies into early-to-mid summer.

before.approach: Drive Hwy 101 to Hoodsport, then SR-119 (North Lake Cushman Road, becomes FR-24 past the lake) roughly 9 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station/trailhead (~800 ft) in the SE corner of Olympic National Park. Hike the North Fork Skokomish River Trail ~3.4 miles to the Spike Camp junction, then climb steeply another ~3.6 miles to Flapjack Lakes (~4,000 ft, 8 miles from the trailhead) — a limited-entry wilderness camping zone, so reserve a permit well ahead. From Flapjack Lakes, continue ~1.5 miles up to Gladys Divide (~5,000 ft), then traverse cross-country toward Sawtooth/Needle Pass to reach the base of The Fin and The Horn. Round-trip approach mileage to Gladys Divide alone runs close to 19 miles with roughly 4,000+ ft of net gain, before the additional ridge travel and the climb itself — this is realistically a backpack-in with a high camp, not a day trip from the road.
before.bail: Reverse the route: rappel or downclimb from the summit notch, traverse back under The Fin's west face to Sawtooth Pass, then descend via Gladys Divide to the Flapjack Lakes trail for the exit — there is no shorter bail option once committed above the notch.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through September - by this point the Putvin Trail approach and Sawtooth high country are reliably snow-free for scrambling.

July.reason: Snow is typically clearing through the month; early July can still have patchy snow on the approach and around the spires, improving toward late July per the best-season window.

June.reason: Lingering snowfields on the steep Putvin Trail headwall and in the high basin are likely; the Class 3-4 rock may still be snow-covered or wet, adding real fall risk on top of already loose terrain.

August.reason: Most reliably dry rock and clearest trail conditions of the season; peak window for the scramble.

October.reason: Early-season snow and increasingly unsettled Olympic weather can return; not covered by the best-season window.

September.reason: Still within the best-season window - dry rock, stable weather, and thinning crowds at the lake.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strong; this is a backpack-in objective, not a day hike. The North Fork Skokomish Trail gains roughly 3,050 ft over about 7-8 miles to Flapjack Lakes camp, then further ascent and off-trail travel via Gladys Divide and Sawtooth Pass to reach The Horn — round-trip mileage to Gladys Divide alone runs close to 19 miles with 4,000+ ft of net gain.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day pack for a fast single-push team; many parties instead carry an overnight kit and camp at Flapjack Lakes to split the approach and climbing into two days.

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long - roughly 7-8 miles and 3,050 ft gain on the North Fork Skokomish Trail to Flapjack Lakes, then further ascent via Gladys Divide and Sawtooth Pass to reach The Horn; realistically a multi-day backpack with a high camp, not a single-push day trip from the road.
requiredSkills: route-finding on an unmaintained, steep boot path and off-trail alpine terrain
comfort with real exposure near the spire summits
steep-snow travel / basic self-arrest if lingering early-season snow is encountered on the approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced scrambler - loose rock and exposure on the Sawtooth spires demand solid Class 3-4 judgment; not a beginner objective.

weather.typical: Warm, drier alpine summer conditions typical of the Olympics' rain-shadow-adjacent southeastern interior during the best-season window.
weather.probability: Afternoon cloud buildup and fast-moving marine fog/weather can move in even in summer; exposed scrambling on The Horn's spires is more consequential if weather turns while up high.

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Significant exposure on the Class 3-4 spire scrambling; loose rock, exposure and rockfall from above mean both a fall and being struck by rockfall from parties above are real consequences in the exposed sections near the summit.

avalanche.zone: Olympics (NWAC forecast zone) - relevant only outside the dry scrambling season; not applicable during the July-September window

pro_tips: Often climbed together with The Fin and other Sawtooth spires
A short rope helps on the exposed sections

waypoints.name: Staircase Ranger Station / North Fork Skokomish Trailhead
waypoints.note: Self-issue wilderness permit at the ranger station kiosk and NW Forest Pass/park entrance fee required for the lot across from the campground.
waypoints.directions: From Hoodsport on Highway 101, take SR-119 (North Lake Cushman Road), which becomes FR-24 past the lake, and follow it roughly 9 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station in the southeast corner of Olympic National Park, around 800 ft. Park in the lot across from the campground — a NW Forest Pass or park entrance fee is required there — and fill out a self-issue wilderness permit at the ranger station kiosk before you start walking. If you plan to camp at Flapjack Lakes, that is a limited-use basin with a reserved permit required from mid-June through September 30, so sort it out well before you drive out.

waypoints.name: Spike Camp junction
waypoints.note: Primitive riverside camp where the North Fork Skokomish River Trail forks toward Flapjack Lakes; last easy river-level water before the steep climb begins.

waypoints.name: Flapjack Lakes
waypoints.note: Established backcountry camp at twin subalpine lakes below Sawtooth Ridge; bear canisters mandatory, camping permit reservation required mid-June-Sept 30, no campfires above 3,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Black and White Lakes junction waterfall
waypoints.note: Waterfall at the Black and White Lakes spur junction is the last reliable, easy water before the dry push toward Gladys Divide.

waypoints.name: Off-trail departure point (~4,400 ft pond)
waypoints.note: Before a small pond on the Gladys Divide trail, leave the maintained tread and head southeast up an open snow/rock slope toward Sawtooth Pass.

waypoints.name: Sawtooth Pass
waypoints.note: Gain the Sawtooth Ridge crest at this saddle, then work along the ridge crest toward the notch below The Fin and The Horn.

waypoints.name: Notch south of The Horn (under The Fin's west face)
waypoints.note: Exposed scramble traverse under The Fin's west face to the notch; loose pillow-basalt and runout (R-rated) moves above the notch onto The Horn.

waypoints.name: The Horn summit
waypoints.note: True summit via the SE or SW 5.5 route from the notch; descend by rappelling from the summit and reversing the traverse under The Fin.
